scenes.heading: A MODEL THAT CANNOT *RAMBLE*
scenes.say: Cloudflare Clef does not write answers at all. It picks from the options you give it — in one pass.
Clef is a twenty seven billion parameter model, post-trained from Qwen three point eight twenty seven B — and it is Apache licensed.
scenes.heading: POST-TRAINED FROM *QWEN3.8-27B*
HOW A *DECISION* MODEL WORKS
scenes.say: You declare the options once. Every question, every allowed choice, gets a probability in a single forward pass. There is no free-form text, and nothing to parse.

scenes.heading: *39 MILLISECONDS* TO DECIDE
scenes.label: clef-flash 9B · community-reported
scenes.say: The flash variant, nine billion parameters, answers in about thirty nine milliseconds by community reports.

scenes.heading: BUILT FOR *SYSTEMONE-STYLE* AGENTS
scenes.say: It is designed to slot into structured decision systems, and it runs on Cloudflare's Workers AI.

scenes.heading: THE *TRADE-OFFS*
scenes.say: The trade-offs: by design it refuses free-form text, you declare every option up front, and a twenty seven billion model needs real hosting. But the flash variant answers in about thirty nine milliseconds, the licence is Apache, and there is no parsing step at all.
Would you put probabilities in your agent instead of paragraphs? Comment Clef and I will pin the model card.

youtube.description:
Cloudflare Clef is a 27B multimodal decision model post-trained from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B. Instead of writing text, a joint schema head returns a probability for every allowed option of every typed question in one forward pass — no output parsing at all. Apache-2.0; clef-flash (9B) runs at ~39 ms median per community reports; Jev/SystemOne compatible; available on Workers AI.
Source: https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef
